mechanism_narrative: Higher housing starts (HOUST) consistently indicate strengthening consumer demand and economic activity, leading to elevated corporate profit expectations and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days without requiring additional conditions.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of months when HOUST exceeds 1400 thousand units, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5%, it signals a restrictive monetary policy that typically causes a short-term pullback in equity valuations due to higher discount rates, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) signals a strong labor market, which typically boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of months when UNRATE falls and PAYEMS rises, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansions (defined by quarterly GDP growth above 2.5% annualized), the S&P 500 typically experiences negative forward returns over the next 60 days due to profit-taking and anticipation of monetary tightening.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when GDPC1 growth exceeds 2.5% annualized, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above 100.5 for two consecutive months signals robust manufacturing activity and economic expansion, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of months when INDPRO > 100.5, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the core CPI (CPIAUCSL) above 260.0 for two consecutive months signals rising inflation, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as the market anticipates aggressive monetary policy.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of months when CPIAUCSL > 260.0, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 6.5% signals a tightening labor market, which typically boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of months when UNRATE < 6.5%, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in retail sales (RSAFS) above 550,000 million dollars for two consecutive months signals strong consumer spending, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of months when RSAFS > 550000, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.
